hook: Great retrieval, sloppy generation = a confident liar with footnotes. This reel: assembling context, forcing citations, and teaching the model to say **“I don’t know.”**

scenes.title: What the model sees is **your design decision**
scenes.sub: Order, format and budget of retrieved context
scenes.narration: Retrieval hands you a list of chunks; the prompt is where they become context. Three design decisions. Order: models attend best to the beginning and end of context — lost-in-the-middle from GA-01 — so place the highest-ranked chunks first and last, burying the middle ones. Format: wrap each chunk in clear delimiters with its source label — doc name, section, date — so the model can cite precisely and tell where context ends and question begins. Budget: reranking gave you five strong chunks; resist the urge to stuff twenty. Context beyond what the question needs dilutes attention and invites the model to synthesize across irrelevant material. Curate the desk; don't empty the archive onto it.

items.s: Best chunks first AND last · the middle is skimmed — design for it
<doc src=…> per chunk → precise citations, clean context/question boundary
5 strong chunks beat 20 padded ones · every extra chunk dilutes attention

scenes.narration: A concrete assembly recipe. Delimiter per chunk with source metadata — that label is what makes citations POSSIBLE. Order: strongest first, second-strongest last, the rest between — because the model's attention is U-shaped. And a budget discipline: if retrieval is confident, five chunks are plenty; if you're adding chunks 'just in case', that's a retrieval-quality problem — go fix GA-15, don't paper over it in assembly. The prompt's system message states the contract: answer only from context, cite every claim, say when information is missing. Assembly is where that contract becomes physically enforceable.

scenes.title: Answers users can **verify** — that's the product
scenes.narration: A grounded answer quotes or closely paraphrases the retrieved context — nothing more. The mechanism: instruct the model to make each claim and attach a citation marker pointing at the source label you provided — [Handbook §4.2, updated March]. Two citation styles: inline markers next to each claim, best for verification; or a sources block at the end, cheaper but weaker. Then the crucial UI move: render citations as links back to the original document. This transforms the chatbot from an oracle into a research assistant — users stop trusting and start VERIFYING, which is exactly what you want, because verification is what makes mistakes survivable.

messages.text: What's our remote-work policy for new joiners?
New joiners work remotely up to 3 days/week after their first 4 weeks, which are fully on-site for onboarding. [People Handbook §7.1 — updated Jun 2026]
Your manager approves via the HR portal; no skip-level sign-off needed. [People Handbook §7.1]

scenes.narration: See how the citation does three jobs at once. Trust: the user can open Handbook section 7.1 and check — no blind faith. Debugging: if the answer is wrong, the citation tells you whether retrieval fetched a stale chunk or the model misread a good one — it separates the two failure families instantly. And compliance: in regulated domains, an answer without a traceable source is unusable regardless of correctness. Notice the second exchange too — the follow-up 'and the approval process' resolved correctly against the same handbook section. That's conversation-awareness, the next chapter: the model inherited context from the first turn instead of treating the follow-up as a brand-new, context-free question.

scenes.title: The highest-value sentence: **“I don’t have that information.”**
scenes.narration: Without guardrails, a language model answers EVERY question — that's its training, not its knowledge. When retrieval returns nothing relevant, the honest response is abstention, and you have to engineer it in. The prompt contract: 'answer only from the context; if the context doesn't contain the answer, say you don't have that information.' Raise the bar in the pipeline: if the best retrieval score is below a threshold, skip the LLM entirely and say nothing was found — a mechanical abstention the model can't overrule. Then evaluate abstention explicitly: in your golden set, include questions the corpus CANNOT answer, and measure whether the system declines them. A RAG system that never says 'I don't know' is lying on a schedule.

items.s: "ONLY the context below… if missing, say so" — the behavioral layer
Best score < threshold → skip the LLM entirely · no model override possible
Golden set MUST include unanswerable questions · measure declines, not just hits

scenes.narration: Layer the defenses. The prompt contract is necessary but insufficient — models under pressure to be helpful will sometimes invent anyway. The mechanical layer removes the temptation: low retrieval confidence short-circuits to 'not found', and no clever wording can talk past a threshold. Then test the negative cases deliberately, because everything in your eval celebrates answers — unanswerable questions are the only way to measure whether honesty holds. Also give abstention a good user experience: 'I couldn't find this in the handbook — want me to search the wider wiki?' An honest system that offers a next step feels helpful, not broken.

scenes.title: Follow-ups are the **real** usage pattern
scenes.sub: Conversation-aware RAG: context isn't just documents
scenes.narration: Nobody asks one perfect question. Real sessions are chains: 'what's the refund policy' → 'and for enterprise customers' → 'how long does that take'. Each follow-up is unanswerable in isolation — 'that' has no referent. Conversation-aware RAG carries state. The standard recipe: keep the chat history, and before retrieval, use an LLM to rewrite the latest question into a standalone query that incorporates the thread — 'what is the refund processing time for enterprise customers'. That rewritten query goes to retrieval; the full history goes to generation, so the answer can stay consistent with what was already said. Skip the rewrite and follow-ups silently degrade into generic answers from mismatched retrieval.

layers.s: Keep the full thread · it's state, not just log
Latest + history → self-contained query (GA-15's rewriter, now conversation-aware)
History + fresh context → consistent, cited answer

scenes.narration: The loop, complete. History feeds the rewriter — the same rewriting machinery from GA-15, now with conversation as its context. Retrieval runs on the STANDALONE query, because vague anaphora like 'that' embeds badly and matches nothing. Generation receives BOTH: the fresh retrieved context and the prior turns, so the answer can refer back — 'as mentioned, enterprise tier differs' — without contradicting itself. Two pitfalls to avoid: unbounded history — trim to the last few turns or summarize, or costs and distraction grow; and staleness — if the conversation pivoted topics, the rewriter must let go of old context instead of dragging it into every new query.

scenes.title: RAG is now solid. Ready to get exotic?
scenes.next: Reel 33 · Advanced RAG — GraphRAG, agentic retrieval, multi-hop, security

recap: Assembly is design: strong chunks first AND last, delimited and source-labeled, curated — never dumped
Citations ([Handbook §7.1]) turn an oracle into a verifiable assistant — and make debugging instant
Abstention is engineered: prompt contract + score threshold + unanswerable questions in the eval; follow-ups need standalone-query rewriting over history

quiz.q: Why place the strongest retrieved chunk at the START and END of context?
opts: Models attend best to context boundaries (lost-in-the-middle) — the middle gets skimmed
Vector databases return them in that order
quiz.why: Attention is U-shaped over long context; assembly order is a free quality dial that exploits it.

quiz.q: What does a mechanical abstention threshold add beyond a prompt contract?
opts: It short-circuits to "not found" before the LLM runs — the model physically can't override it
quiz.why: Prompts are requests; thresholds are gates. Low retrieval confidence → no generation call at all.

quiz.q: Why rewrite follow-up questions before retrieval?
opts: Anaphora like "that" embeds badly and matches nothing — the rewrite makes it a standalone query
quiz.why: Retrieval needs a self-contained query; the rewrite resolves references against chat history so embedding space contains something to match.

code.title: Generation stage: assembly, citations, abstention, follow-ups
code.body:
SYSTEM = """You are a helpful assistant. Rules:
1. Answer ONLY from the <context> below.
2. Cite every claim as [source-label].
3. If the context lacks the answer, say exactly:
   "I don't have that information."
Never use outside knowledge."""

def ask(history: list[dict], question: str) -> str:
    # 1 · follow-up → standalone query
    standalone = llm(
        "Rewrite as a self-contained search query.",
        history=history, question=question)

    # 2 · retrieve (GA-15 stack)
    chunks = retrieve(standalone, k=5)

    # 3 · mechanical abstention — before any LLM call
    if not chunks or chunks[0].score < 0.62:
        return "I couldn't find that in the handbook. Search the wider wiki?"

    # 4 · assemble: best first AND last (U-shaped attention)
    ordered = [chunks[0], *chunks[1:], chunks[0]] if len(chunks) > 2 else chunks
    context = "\n".join(
        f'<doc src="{c.source}">{c.text}</doc>' for c in ordered)

    # 5 · generate with history + grounded context
    return chat(SYSTEM, history + [
        {"role": "user",
         "content": f"<context>\n{context}\n</context>\n\n{standalone}"}])
annot: Abstention gate sits BEFORE the expensive call — cost saving and honesty in one mechanism
Duplicating the top chunk at the end exploits U-shaped attention; with ≤2 chunks it's a no-op
History goes to generation, standalone query goes to retrieval — each gets the input it's built for

notes:
# Generation & Citations

## Context assembly
- Attention is U-shaped → strongest chunk first AND last.
- Delimit each chunk: `<doc src="label">…` → enables precise citation.
- Curate ~5 chunks; padding = retrieval problem, fix GA-15.

## Grounded answers & citations
- Every claim carries a source marker; UI renders it as a link.
- Citations = trust + debuggability (retrieval-fail vs read-fail) + compliance.

## “I don't know”
- Prompt contract + score-threshold gate + unanswerable questions in the golden set.
- Good UX: abstain + offer a next step.

## Conversation-aware RAG
- Rewrite follow-up → standalone query (history-aware), retrieve on it.
- Generation sees history + fresh context → consistent answers.
- Pitfalls: unbounded history (trim/summarize), stale topics (rewriter must pivot).
